definitions.explanation: going easy; holding back; pulling one's punches; moderation

examples.japanese: {手加減|てかげん}⟦しないで→する：00392_suru⟧。
{子|こ}ども⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{手加減|てかげん}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んだ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: I went easy on them since they were children.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{手加減|てかげん}⟦{抜|ぬ}き→抜き：23505_nuki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{勝負|しょうぶ}→勝負：01437_shoubu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{挑|いど}んだ→挑む：12708_idomu⟧。
examples.english: He went into the match without holding back.

notes:
{手加減|てかげん} literally means "hand adjustment" and refers to moderating one's strength or effort, typically to avoid causing harm or to match an opponent's level.

Common expressions:
- {手加減|てかげん}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to go easy, to hold back)
- {手加減|てかげん}なし / {手加減|てかげん}⟦{抜|ぬ}き→抜き：23505_nuki⟧ (without holding back, full force)
- {手加減|てかげん}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦もらう→もらう：00520_morau⟧ (to have someone go easy on you)

Contexts:
- Sports/games: adjusting effort when playing against weaker opponents
- Criticism/feedback: softening criticism to be less harsh
- Physical activities: not using full strength
